title: nonblocking-tool-fanout-and-safety-modes-prd-wip
content:
Summary
This doc proposes a design for nonblocking tool-call fanout modes and a small set of safety modes for the Hosted API streaming surface. Goal: enable fast user-visible partial results by allowing the model to emit structured tool-invocation signals that can be dispatched to one or more downstream tool endpoints asynchronously, while preserving developer ergonomics in SDKs and minimizing accidental unsafe operations.

Why this now
- Customers want lower tail latency for first actionable content (partial answers + tool outputs).
- Current blocking tool-call semantics (model pauses for tool response) forces long sync waits and hurts UX for mobile/low-bandwidth clients.
- We currently lack a clear surface for multi-tool fanout (call search + db + external API in parallel) and for safe defaults when tools have side effects.

Nonblocking fanout: high-level idea
- Model emits structured tool invocation frames in the stream (tool_call_frame) describing: tool_id, version, inputs, urgency_hint, expected_result_schema, safety_mode_hint, correlation_id.
- Client SDK (or server router) can choose immediate nonblocking dispatch to configured tool endpoints, or buffer + batch, or convert to optimistic local shim.
- Model continues generation without blocking for tool responses; partial tool results are streamed back later and can be stitched into the main transcript as separate frames.
- Developers can opt-in to stitching semantics (auto-merge tool outputs into the main response) or receive tool outputs as separate events to handle themselves.

Safety modes (a minimal taxonomy)
- read-only: calls that must not mutate external state (safe default for most third-party functions).
- conditional-write: call may mutate state only if the client explicitly confirms (two-phase commit style).
- fire-and-forget-write: immediate side-effecting calls where client accepted full responsibility (dangerous — require enterprise opt-in).
- sandboxed-simulate: run tool in a sandboxed simulation; return only simulated output labelled clearly.

Design constraints and heuristics
- Backwards compatibility: existing blocking tool-call API must keep working. Introduce a new streaming frame type rather than replace current frames.
- Minimal server-side policy surface: safety mode enforcement should be opt-in per-customer config (default read-only).
- Latency-first: nonblocking fanout must not add extra round-trips for the main generation path.
- Observability: every tool_call_frame must emit a token-level telemetry event with correlation_id to make trace stitching possible.
- SDK ergonomics: clients should have three lines of code to adopt default safe behavior. Advanced users can swap in custom interceptors.

Protocol sketch (stream frames)
- tool_call_frame (streamed): {"type":"tool_call","tool":"search.v2","inputs":{...},"urgency":"background|foreground","safety":"read-only|conditional-write|fire-and-forget|simulate","expected_schema":"application/json+shapes/v1","corr_id":"uuid"}
- tool_result_frame (streamed): {"type":"tool_result","corr_id":"uuid","status":"ok|error|timed_out|skipped","payload_type":"json|text|attachment","payload":"...","source":"tool-endpoint-id","latency_ms":"123"}
- note: above are conceptual; actual wire uses compact keys for bandwidth.

Server routing behavior
- Router inspects tool_call_frame and policy map: if tool endpoint available in same region and safety policy allows, dispatch; else fallback to queued dispatch or simulate mode.
- Implement admission gating: if a customer has not enabled write mode for a tool, router downgrades to sandboxed-simulate automatically and streams a tool_result_frame with status "simulated".

SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile)
- Default client behavior (safe, zero-config): on receiving tool_call_frame with safety != fire-and-forget, queue a local stub that returns a placeholder and present an event stream to app: onToolInvocation(toolMeta, respondFn). The SDK emits tool_result_frame when the tool returns.
- Stitching helper: SDK exposes a small transformer: stitchToolResults(transcript, toolEvents) -> merged transcript with provenance markers. This is provided as a library util rather than default behavior.
- Async listener API: app can register handlers: registerToolHandler(toolId, handlerFn) where handlerFn returns a Promise. If handler takes > threshold, SDK optionally shows progressive UI.
- Low-bandwidth mode: SDK can compress payloads and defer non-urgent tool calls (urgency hint).

Developer UX patterns
- Pattern A (safe immediate): default for most apps. Nonblocking fanout for read-only tools; app receives tool_result_frame and can update UI when ready. No state mutation occurs automatically.
- Pattern B (confirm-before-write): Model suggests an action (conditional-write). App shows a confirm modal with model text + source confidence; on user confirm, the SDK calls an explicit action endpoint to complete the write.
- Pattern C (parallel fanout): for latency-heavy read-only workflows, the system fans out to multiple tools (search + summary + metadata) and aggregates the first N results. Aggregation is done by the app or by a server-side combiner component.

Observability and debugging
- Correlation ids: every model request gets a root request id and each tool_call_frame has a corr_id. We must ensure these are indexed in Console.
- Telemetry surface: tool dispatch latency, tool success rate, simulator fallback rate, safety-downgrades per customer, token attribution for partial content.
- Console UX: per-session timeline view that shows main generation tokens interleaved with tool events (collapsible). Must support filter by tool and safety mode.

Security and compliance notes
- Side-effecting tools require review and opt-in at account level. We must provide a clear audit trail for all write-mode tool invocations.
- KMS/HSM integration for signing tool dispatches for on-prem Private deployments.
- Data residency: tool dispatch should respect customer routing policies (no cross-region dispatch for private customers unless explicitly allowed).

Rollout plan (phased)
- Phase 0: internal experiment — enable nonblocking frames for a small set of read-only tools; collect telemetry. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1: public beta for customers with feature flag. Default safety = read-only. SDK helpers published (JS + Python). (4 sprints)
- Phase 2: conditional-write flows and confirm-before-write UX patterns, Console audit trail and per-customer safety toggles. (3 sprints)
- Phase 3: enterprise opt-in fire-and-forget + on-prem tool signing. (2–4 sprints, gated by legal/review)

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Should we do server-side automatic combiner/aggregator for parallel fanout or leave aggregation to apps? Tradeoff: developer simplicity vs control and cost.
- How aggressive should safety downgrades be? (Default to simulate or to not dispatch?)
- Bandwidth: how do we keep streaming footprint small on mobile for many small tool-result frames? Consider compact binary frames.
- Authorization model for downstream tool endpoints: per-tool tokens vs router-signed delegation tokens.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative on safety defaults. We want to avoid accidental writes.
- Focus review on SDK ergonomics (would three lines of code feel natural?) and Console telemetry needs.
- Related PRs: see linked artifacts. TODOs: add data model shape examples, draft JS SDK snippets, add sample session transcript with interleaved frames.

Appendix: short example transcript (conceptual)
- client -> POST /v1/streams generate -> stream tokens: "Here are some options:\n1) Search for recent pricing\n[tool_call: {tool:search.v2, inputs:{q:\"pricing for rtx40\"}, urgency:\"foreground\", safety:\"read-only\", corr_id:\"c1\"}]\n2) Summarize\n"
- Stream later: tool_result_frame corr_id c1: payload {top_hit:..., latency_ms:240}
- model continues and emits final answer referencing search results.

-- end --
